articleText: Anthropic strikes $3.4B generator deal to secure data center power: FT (ANT:Pending) Seeking Alpha
reactions: [Hacker News] It's the other way around: renewables come first, AI boom comes second. That's why, despite the initial lead, US has already lost the AI race. For the next decade or two US AI companies will be tied in legal fights over electricity demands of their data centers, while China, having abundance of electricity will build hundreds of AI data centers and leapfrog US.
[Hacker News] Scaling renewables is slow Not in China. They have as much renewable energy capacity in place as the rest of the world combined.

[Hacker News] Isn't this fairly close to what rationalist AI cultists say? That we should pour all resources into creating an AI god above all else, because that would save the largest number of people if you also include those that aren't born yet? It hardly sounds like sarcasm.

[Hacker News] What truly drives me crazy is that if they ran a slower build-out, at a pace that allowed supporting industries (manufacturing of dram, electrical infrastructure) to grow at a sustainable rate, the impact would manageable. You can make data-centers that don't waste water, that use renewable energy, that aren't titanic eye and audio sores on their communities; it's just more expensiv

[Hacker News] True. But most are in the east? The most expensive land? Near the coast? I have a hard time believing that. I think most are in the west, where energy land water is cheap and the climate cool. I have seen the datacenters in Guizhou with my own eyes and its insane. Now they are expanding to Inner-Mongolia and also in (sub tropical!) Guangdong specifically for AI datacenters.
